seoTitle: How to Use the Outline Tool in Google Docs (2026)
metaDescription: Enable the Google Docs outline sidebar to navigate long documents by heading, jump between sections instantly, and manage headings on the fly.
intro: Long documents become much easier to navigate once you turn on the outline sidebar. This guide covers revealing the outline panel, applying heading styles so sections populate it automatically, and using outline links to jump between parts of a lengthy manual, thesis, or strategy document instead of scrolling endlessly.

steps.heading: Reveal the outline sidebar
steps.body: Open the View menu and enable Show outline to display the document outline panel alongside your text.

steps.heading: Apply heading styles
steps.body: Use Heading 1, Heading 2, and Heading 3 styles on your section titles so they automatically populate the outline panel.

steps.heading: Add or remove headings from the panel
steps.body: Manage entries directly from the outline view without needing to change your underlying document copy.

steps.heading: Navigate with outline links
steps.body: Click any entry in the outline panel to jump straight to that section, no matter how long the document is.

steps.heading: Use the summary box
steps.body: Add a brief overview in the summary box snippet at the top of the outline panel to track project goals and updates.

steps.heading: Check outline access on mobile
steps.body: The outline tool is also available in the Google Docs mobile app on Android and iOS for reviewing structure on the go.

faq.question: Why isn't my document showing anything in the outline panel?
faq.answer: The outline populates based on heading styles; make sure your section titles use Heading 1, 2, or 3 rather than plain bold text.

faq.question: Can I remove a heading from the outline without deleting the text?
faq.answer: Yes, you can remove entries from the outline panel itself without changing the formatting or content in your document body.

faq.question: Is the outline tool available on mobile devices?
faq.answer: Yes, the outline feature works within the Google Docs mobile app on both Android and iOS.

faq.question: Does the outline tool work like a table of contents?
faq.answer: It functions similarly for navigation purposes, though the outline panel is a sidebar tool rather than an inserted element in the document itself.
